component_policy.work_ids: stable local keys, unique within the plicanon namespace; non-semantic labels. The 80 imported mnemonic ids are retained by Gate B decision B3, including 16 that echo a commentary layer; an id is never evidence of classification or relationship
component_policy.version_ids: one atomic registered CTS VERSION token per distinct textual expression, matching ^v[0-9]{4,}$; no dot-separated source/language/translator subfields
component_policy.exemplar_ids: one atomic registered CTS EXEMPLAR token per specific copy/item of a version when item-level identity matters, matching ^x[0-9]{4,}$
component_policy.identifier_character_profile: lowercase ASCII letters, digits, and underscore; no periods or CTS-reserved delimiters inside a single identifier token
component_policy.passage_colon: required even when the passage component is empty
component_policy.passage_validation: full CTS parser plus registered per-work citation model; lexical regex alone is not conformance

namespace_authority_policy.requirement: The CTS namespace token must resolve through the namespace catalog to one stable authority URI.
namespace_authority_policy.resolver_endpoints: Maintain separately from the authority URI and allow endpoint migration without changing URNs.

short_token_candidate.reason: A short CTS namespace token is not an authority URI; adopting it would create a separate namespace-token migration and requires stewardship/governance approval.

recension_identity_policy.classification_only_difference: Never creates a new Work; encode scoped collection-membership and textual-role assertions.
recension_identity_policy.shared_model_test: Test S (spec 2.9.2) yields yes/no/uncertain. yes requires a reviewed model, zero unevaluated nodes and an unresolved fraction at or below the steward-set parameter; no requires a reviewer finding of structural irreconcilability with evidence; everything else is uncertain.
recension_identity_policy.textual_difference_with_shared_reference: Verdict yes: new Version under the same Work, with mappings and lineage metadata.
recension_identity_policy.separate_work_threshold: Verdict no, or verdict yes with a documented distinct referential scope: separate Work records, an approved Identity Decision Record and a reviewed relation.
recension_identity_policy.uncertainty: Verdict uncertain or missing evidence: HOLD. The smallest affected identifier set stays unminted (minting_state held_uncertain); no provisional public split.
recension_identity_policy.identity_stability: Published URNs keep their referents; mappings may be revised with provenance; shared-model changes after minting are additive only.

resolver_fallback_policy.permitted_fallback: A resolver may offer a separately identified candidate with its own URN, reason, and relation/alignment status; it must not present it as the requested exact text.

registry.schema_file_status: paired_draft_artifact; schema $id uses the reserved example.invalid domain until a public schema location is chosen

identity_parameters.note: Set by the steward at Gate A on 2026-10-10. A model with fewer than 20 nodes tolerates no unresolved node (one uncertain node already exceeds 5%).

token_policy.work_ids: Retained by Gate B decision B3 (option a): the 80 mnemonic ids stay as non-semantic keys, including the 16 whose ids end in a, mht or pmt. An id is a label, never a claim; commentary relations are carried by reviewed relationships, not by the id.
token_policy.version_exemplar_ids: Normative by Gate B decision B4. No semantics; metadata corrections never change a minted token.

findings: The selected authority URI is the versioned resolver PURL. The spec says the authority URI 'need not be the active API endpoint', so this is permitted; the risk is that a service version (v1) sits inside a permanent identifier.
The PURL service allows a single maintainer per domain, so the succession statement needs a procedure for transferring the PURL maintainer role as well as the committee hand-over.
The declared fallback endpoint returned 404 and is not independent of the PURL service, so it cannot be recorded as an independent fallback.
The resolver endpoint answers with a plain-text stub, not a CTS protocol response (a Gate D matter).
The catalog PURL still targets a mutable branch reference (refs/heads/main); no tagged release or digest exists yet.
The durability statement describes hosting that was not observed: the PURL service stores redirects only, the resolver and catalog are hosted elsewhere, and no mirror was seen.
The file named as holding the durability statement (plicanon_gate_status_v4_4_prep_rev3.json) is not part of the bundle or of anything supplied in this review.
missing: An independent fallback endpoint, or a decision to rely on PURL retargeting as the continuity mechanism
A tagged release for the catalog and its SHA-256 digest, with the PURL retargeted to the tag
Evidence that the named successor accepts the role
A procedure for transferring the PURL domain maintainer role
A durability statement that matches the observed hosting, or the hosting changes to match the statement

textgroups.label: Pāli textual-work inventory
textgroups.purpose: A stable organizational container, not a claim about canonical status, genre, textual genealogy, or tradition membership.

citation_models.note: Standard scholarly reference is PTS volume.page (concordance layer only).
Passage component does not repeat the work identifier.

classification_schemes.label: Literary form
classification_schemes.scope_rule: An assertion may describe a work, a part of a work, or one edition; scope must be explicit when it is not the whole work.

classification_schemes.label: Collection or tradition membership
classification_schemes.scope_rule: Every membership assertion must name the tradition/collection and evidence or source; no global canonical=true/false field.

classification_schemes.label: Textual role
classification_schemes.scope_rule: Role claims such as commentary, sub-commentary, grammar, chronicle, or manual are classifications; relations to a specific target work are separate records.

classification_schemes.label: Original v3 textgroup assignment
classification_schemes.scope_rule: Historical migration provenance only; not used to construct v4 URNs.

classification_schemes.label: Original v3 genre assignment
classification_schemes.scope_rule: Historical migration provenance only; no assertion is assumed verified.

relationship_types.meaning: The subject work comments on the target work.
The subject work is a sub-commentary on the target work.
The subject work is a translation of the target work.
The subject work quotes the target work.
The subject work is explicitly claimed to derive from the target work.
An editorial assertion of work-level identity; requires evidence and review.
A broad symmetric relation that makes no claim of identity or equivalence.
The subject is registered as a distinct textual recension related to a broader work record.

identifier_examples.note: Textgroup-level CTS URN. The empty passage component is expressed by the required final colon.
Work-level URN. It does not claim an edition or specific passage.
Shared logical passage address; content retrieval must disclose or explicitly select a concrete version.
Version-level passage. The version token must be backed by a complete, reviewed version record before it is mintable/resolvable.
Exemplar-level passage. The exemplar must identify one specific item/copy of the registered version; it is not merely another source/language subfield.

legacy_migration.policy: Never reinterpret version and exemplar components by guesswork. Preserve old identifiers as aliases when they have been published; add a fully explicit mapping where semantics are known.
legacy_migration.safe_rule: Versionless old work URNs can be mapped from their old textgroup to pali when the work identifier and passage model have been verified.
legacy_migration.unsafe_rule: Version-qualified URNs such as sutta.dn.pts.pli must not be automatically rewritten as version=pts_pli: CTS parses pts as VERSION and pli as EXEMPLAR under the standard four-level hierarchy.
legacy_migration.publication_gate: Before public minting, inventory all previously published v2/v3 URNs and freeze permanent aliases. If v3 URNs have already been cited, do not treat this draft as permission to change their meaning.

v4_1_policy.namespace_token: Keep plicanon in all proposed v4.1 URNs; do not rewrite to pli without a separately approved namespace migration.
v4_1_policy.version_exemplar_interpretation: Legacy dotted strings are interpreted under CTS ordering first. Never reinterpret source/language/translator dots as a composite VERSION unless a curated, provenance-bearing migration record proves that historic software used a non-CTS interpretation.
v4_1_policy.fallback: Never redirect an ambiguous or unavailable legacy reference to an arbitrary nearest passage or default witness.

v4_2_policy.alias_records: Every known published legacy URN gets a legacy_aliases record: mapped, quarantined_ambiguous, or rejected.
v4_2_policy.ambiguous: Quarantined forms resolve to an explicit ambiguity response, never to a default or nearest target.
v4_2_policy.no_published_urns_known: Gate C stays open until the audit result is recorded, including a recorded result of none.

urn_syntax.passage_delimiter: A final colon is required even when PASSAGE is empty.
